title: Sheafification of an affine quotient resolution
statement: Let i:Z\to Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme], U an affine open of Y, A=\Gamma(Y,U), and I an ideal of A. Assume an isomorphism e:i^{-1}(U)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(A/I) identifies i|_U followed by U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A with e followed by the quotient-spectrum map. Let K_\bullet be an arbitrary nonnegative chain complex of A-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] and let \epsilon:K_\bullet\to(A/I)[0] be a quasi-isomorphism, meaning it induces an isomorphism on every homology module. Then there exists a quasi-isomorphism from the termwise associated-sheaf complex transported along the affine chart U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A to ((i_*\mathcal O_Z)|_U)[0]. No bound, finiteness or regularity assumption on K_\bullet is required.

source.place: Tag 068C, Lemma 37.61.7, affine finite free resolution argument; affine-local quotient identification and sheafification

proof.text: Identify the associated quotient sheaf on the affine chart with the restricted structure-sheaf pushforward using affine_quotient_restricted_iso. This statement concerns module sheaves only, independently of any resolution or chain complex.

The fully faithful left-adjoint tilde functor preserves cokernels and is additive. The kernel of a morphism of its images is quasi-coherent, hence lies in its essential image by the affine quasi-coherent counit isomorphism. Pull the kernel cone back using full faithfulness. The mapped cone is isomorphic to the original kernel cone, and full faithfulness reflects its universal property. Consequently tilde preserves kernels, hence finite limits. It already preserves finite colimits as a left adjoint.

Restriction along the affine chart isomorphism preserves finite limits and colimits. Their composite with tilde is therefore an exact additive functor, so Mathlib maps the augmentation to a quasi-isomorphism. Compose with the natural isomorphism comparing the mapped single complex to the single complex of the mapped quotient module, then with the single complex of the module isomorphism from the first step. Isomorphisms and composition preserve quasi-isomorphisms, giving the required witness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 068C affine resolution argument; categorical exactness realized using the proved quasi-coherent kernel theorem and Mathlib exact-functor machinery instead of a new stalkwise exactness proof.

theorem exists_affine_quotient_sheafified_resolution {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (U : Y.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (I : Ideal (Γ(Y, U)))
    (e : Scheme.Opens.toScheme (i ⁻¹ᵁ U) ≅
      Spec (CommRingCat.of ((Γ(Y, U) : Type u) ⧸ I)))
    (he : i ∣_ U ≫ U.toSpecΓ =
      e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
    (K : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(Y, U) : Type u)) ℕ)
    (ε : K ⟶ (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat (Γ(Y, U) : Type u))).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (Γ(Y, U) : Type u) ((Γ(Y, U) : Type u) ⧸ I)))
    [QuasiIso ε] :
    ∃ q : ((tilde.functor Γ(Y, U) ⋙
          Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor hU.isoSpec.hom).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj K ⟶
        (ChainComplex.single₀ U.toScheme.Modules).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))),
      QuasiIso q
